title: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5.5 with 1M context — Venture Herald
text:
Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5.5 on September 28, 2026, positioning it as the second model in its Claude 5.5 family. The company says the new model is its best combination of speed and intelligence, with a 1 million-token context window, a 128,000-token maximum output and pricing set at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.

Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5.5 on September 28, 2026, according to its release notes, and later documented the model’s pricing, limits and platform availability in its product docs. The company positions Sonnet 5.5 as the second model in the Claude 5.5 family, following Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22, 2026 and ahead of Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7, 2026.

...

Claude Sonnet 5.5 gives developers a 1 million-token context window and a 128,000-token maximum output, according to Anthropic’s model overview. In practical terms, the larger context window lets teams feed in much longer documents, codebases or conversation histories before the model has to drop earlier material. The output cap also allows for long responses, including extended code generation or analysis.

...

## How much does Claude Sonnet 5.5 cost?

Anthropic lists Claude Sonnet 5.5 at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. It also says the model’s prompt-caching prices are $2.50 per million tokens for a five-minute cache write, $4 per million for a one-hour cache write and $0.10 per million for cache reads.

The company says the model has the same prices as Claude Sonnet 5 except for prompt cache reads, which cost half as much on Sonnet 5.5 at $0.10 per million tokens. Anthropic also says the Batch API offers a 50% discount on input and output pricing.

For some batch workflows, Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 supports up to 300,000 output tokens on the Message Batches API with a beta header. The minimum cacheable prompt length is 512 tokens.

## Where is Claude Sonnet 5.5 available?

Anthropic says Claude Sonnet 5.5 is available to all Claude API customers under the identifier claude-sonnet-5-5, and it is also available through Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry. The overview page also lists Claude Platform on AWS among the supported platforms.

Anthropic provides platform-specific model IDs as well. For Amazon Bedrock, the model ID is anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5, and for Microsoft Foundry it is claude-sonnet-5-5. The company says the model launched on September 28, 2026 and will not retire sooner than September 28, 2027.

...

For Sonnet 5.5 specifically, Anthropic says it runs 30%+ faster than Claude Sonnet 5 and costs up to 30% less for most work.

title: Anthropic cuts Sonnet 5.5 cache-read price by half
text:
# Anthropic cuts Sonnet 5.5 cache-read price by half

Anthropic says reads of stored material cost $0.10 per million tokens, down from $0.20, while input and output rates stay at $2 and $10 per million tokens.

By AveNews SI desk

10 November 2026

SI

Sole source: Anthropic. The company says its Claude Sonnet 5.5 model halves the price of reading cached material compared with Sonnet 5. Cache reads cost $0.10 per million tokens, down from $0.20; ordinary input and output prices remain unchanged. The company says the model also typically uses fewer tokens to do the same work.

Tokens are units used to measure the text a model processes or generates. A cache stores material for reuse, so the lower rate applies when that stored material is read again. Anthropic says its own tests found Sonnet 5.5 cost up to 30% less per task than its predecessor; that is separate from the fixed reduction in the cache-read rate.

## Costs depend on the task and settings

The company positions the model for defined everyday tasks such as fixing bugs and making documents, slides and spreadsheets. It presents Sonnet 5.5 as a faster, lower-cost complement to Opus 5.5, which it says remains stronger at complex, open-ended work requiring sustained judgment.

...

Anthropic says users who run Sonnet with thinking turned off must switch to the between_tools setting before moving to the new model; that setting keeps up-front thinking off. The company says higher-risk cybersecurity tasks will visibly fall back to Sonnet 5, while users can still find and fix bugs in routine software development.

Anthropic says cyberdefenders will soon be able to apply to its expanded Cyber Verification Program for tiered access to more advanced capabilities on Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Claude Mythos models. It also plans to add Haiku 5.5, intended for high-volume and cost-sensitive applications, in the coming weeks.

title: Anthropic Launches Claude Haiku 5.5 and Cuts Sonnet 5.5 Pricing | Hermes Vector
text:
AI & SI November 12, 2026

# Anthropic Launches Claude Haiku 5.5 and Cuts Sonnet 5.5 Pricing

Anthropic introduces Claude Haiku 5.5, its fastest and cheapest small model, and lowers cache read prices for Claude Sonnet 5.5.

By Hermes Vector

## In brief

- Anthropic introduces Claude Haiku 5.5 as its cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model.
- Haiku 5.5 costs around 75% less to run on average than Haiku 4.5.
- Cache reads for Claude Sonnet 5.5 are halved to $0.10 per million tokens.
- Haiku 5.5 is available on Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

# Anthropic Launches Claude Haiku 5.5 and Cuts Sonnet 5.5 Pricing

Anthropic has introduced Claude Haiku 5.5, which it describes as the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model it has released. The model is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks such as summaries, database queries, and classification requests.

## Performance and Pricing

Anthropic says Haiku 5.5 costs around 75% less to run on average than Haiku 4.5. The company also announced a 50% reduction in cache read prices for Claude Sonnet 5.5, lowering the cost to $0.10 per million tokens from $0.20. This change makes Sonnet 5.5 around 20% cheaper on most agentic work.

The source includes a benchmark table comparing Haiku 5.5, Haiku 4.5, and Sonnet 5.5 across knowledge work, computer use, multidisciplinary reasoning, agentic coding, and visual reasoning. For example, on OSWorld 2.1 offline subset, Haiku 5.5 scored 72.4%, compared with 15.7% for Haiku 4.5 and 83.9% for Sonnet 5.5. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Haiku 5.5 scored 39.2%, compared with 0.0% for Haiku 4.5 and 70.6% for Sonnet 5.5.

...

Customers including Asana, HubSpot, AlphaSense, Box, Rogo, and Cognition provided feedback. Asana reported over a 30% reduction in latency for task completions and up to 2.5x faster inference per agent turn. HubSpot said Haiku 5.5 achieved a 92.8% average score on its CRM evaluation suite across three runs.

Claude Haiku 5.5 is available now on Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. On the Claude Platform, developers can use claude-haiku-5-5.

## Why it matters

The launch gives developers a lower-cost, faster option for high-volume tasks, while the Sonnet 5.5 price cut reduces expenses for agentic workloads. New monthly API credits for Max, Ultra, and Team subscribers are also being rolled out to support building agents and applications on the Claude Platform.

title: Sonnet 4.5 Retires Nov 30: Migration Saves Only 13% • The Weighted Average
text:
Anthropic retires Claude Sonnet 4.5 on November 30, 2026, and requests to the retired model fail after that date. The replacement, Sonnet 5.5, lists one-third lower per token. Anthropic’s own tokenizer note cuts that advantage to about 13% on the same text, so the deadline is a migration project with a thin margin, not a windfall.

## A one-third list cut, trimmed by the tokenizer

Anthropic’s pricing page lists Sonnet 4.5 at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. Sonnet 5.5 lists at $2 and $10, and its cache reads drop from $0.30 to $0.10 per million tokens. On the rate card alone, every category falls by a third or more.

Rate cards compare prices per token, and a token is not a fixed unit across model generations. The same page says Claude 4.7 and later models use a newer tokenizer that “produces approximately 30% more tokens for the same text,” with the exact increase depending on content and workload. Sonnet 5.5 belongs to that later group. To compare like with like, scale each Sonnet 5.5 price by 1.30 so it prices the same text Sonnet 4.5 would have tokenized:

- Input: $2 × 1.30 = $2.60, against $3.00. A 13.3% saving.
- Output: $10 × 1.30 = $13.00, against $15.00. Also 13.3%.
- Cache reads: $0.10 × 1.30 = $0.13, against $0.30. A 57% saving.

The 33% headline is the list cut; the tokenizer math below shows what survives. Two more pricing-page rules change the arithmetic for some teams. Regional and multi-region endpoints on partner clouds carry a 10% premium that applies to Sonnet 4.5 and later alike, so it leaves the ratio intact. The US-only inference option is different: the page says it applies a 1.1x multiplier to Claude 4.6 and later models. A team that needs US-only inference and moves to Sonnet 5.5 gives back that multiplier. Input becomes $2 × 1.30 × 1.10 = $2.86, against $3.00, a saving of about 4.7%.

...

Any workload pinned to `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` has to move before November 30. Anthropic’s model deprecations page names Sonnet 5.5 as the replacement and says that requests past the retirement date fail. The migration guide covers the code changes, and the models overview lists Sonnet 5.5 as active, with no retirement before September 28, 2027. The notice dates from September 30, so most teams have had two months to start and roughly four weeks remain.

title: Claude Price Changes Since 2024: What Went Up and Why
text:
Claude list prices moved both ways since March 2024. Opus fell from $15 / $75 to $4 / $20 per 1M tokens, Sonnet fell from $3 / $15 to $2 / $10 after one listing that rose to $6 / $30, and Haiku rose once, then dropped to $0.1 / $0.5. Per task, Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 are the expensive Claude options today, and the plan-versus-API answer depends on how many agent runs you do.

Note that these are first-seen prices for each model version, and only a few older models have a later listing. Three patterns stand out:

- Opus got cheaper. The first three Opus versions were $15 / $75. Opus 4.5 cut that to $5 / $25, and Opus 5.5 went to $4 / $20.
- Sonnet had one clear increase. The Claude 3.5 Sonnet listing changed from $3 / $15 to $6 / $30 on 2026-03-30. Sonnet 5 then arrived at $2 / $10 in July 2026.
- Haiku rose, then fell. Claude 3.5 Haiku launched at $1 / $5, up from $0.25 / $1.25 for Claude 3 Haiku. Its latest listing is $0.8 / $4, and Haiku 5.5 launched at $0.1 / $0.5.

title: Claude Haiku vs Sonnet: 5.5 pricing, routing and reasoning tradeoffs · Headless Thrones
text:
Haiku lists $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens. Above that prompt length, the listed rates become $0.50 and $2.50. Sonnet lists $2 input and $10 output per million tokens. A comparison that prints only Haiku’s lowest rate without the threshold would mislead long-document users. Haiku specifications and pricing, Sonnet specifications and pricing.

For an illustrative batch totaling two million uncached input tokens and 500,000 billed output tokens, Haiku costs $0.45 if each prompt stays within the lower tier, or $2.25 if every request qualifies for the higher tier. Sonnet costs $9 under its stated standard rates. A mixed batch must be calculated request by request. These figures omit cache operations, tools, discounts, taxes and retries, and include whatever reasoning is billed as output.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Sonnet 4.6 with 1 million token context — ProArena.net
text:
Anthropic presented Claude Sonnet 4.6 - an updated version of its “average” model, which is already approaching the level of Opus in a number of tasks.

Sonnet 4.6 is now the default model in claude.ai and Claude Cowork for Free and Pro users. The price remains the same: from $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens - the same as Sonnet 4.5.

The main update is a context window of 1 million tokens (currently in beta mode). This is a volume that can accommodate an entire repository, a long contract, or dozens of scientific articles. It is important that the model does not just accept a large amount of text, but is capable of maintaining logical connections throughout the request and planning actions over a long horizon.
